text:
maria: heads up — seeing a burst of gpu nodes in gpu-pool-3 flipping to NotReady and getting tainted NoSchedule. started ~10:12 UTC. pods with GPUs are stuck Pending.

maria: quick kubectl snapshot:
```
kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-pool-3
ip-10-0-3-21   NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   1/1     Ready    2d
ip-10-0-3-22   NotReady                       0/1     Ready    3h

kubectl describe pod nvidia-device-plugin-abc -n kube-system
Events:
  Warning  Failed   2m (x5 over 3m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-3-21  Failed to attach device: handshake timeout with nvidia kernel module
  Warning  BackOff  1m (x3 over 2m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-3-21  Back-off restarting failed container
```

ken: ugh. any recent driver rollout? did the daemonset update yesterday finish?

maria: we rolled a driver image last night (nv-driver:2026-03-17b) across all pools. rollout reported success but looks like some nodes never loaded the kernel module and device-plugin is hitting a hard failure path.

ash: cluster-autoscaler is also not scaling up because pods are matching nodeSelector/tolerations that no available node satisfies. autoscaler logs show: 
```
I0325 10:15:00 scaler.go:... ScaleUp: rejected - no template matching tolerations/taints
```

infra-bot: [ALERT] 6 nodes in gpu-pool-3 marked NotReady by kubelet (reason: DriverInitTimeout). Pager routed to eng-infra.

samir: can we try a staged daemonset restart? if we restart driver ds across all nodes at once we blow up the pool. prefer sequential: cordon a node, drain (ignore daemonsets), patch ds image on that node, uncordon.

jess: agree with staged. likely root cause is new driver image triggers modprobe that hangs on some kernel variants (we saw this with the 5.15->5.19 kernel drift). device-plugin expects /proc/driver/nvidia ready, but init is timing out.

ken: can you paste the kubelet logs where it marks NotReady?

maria: small excerpt:
```
Mar 18 10:13:12 kubelet[1234]: E0318 10:13:12 kernel_mod_probe.go:78] modprobe error: exit status 1 (timeout)
Mar 18 10:13:12 kubelet[1234]: E0318 10:13:12 device_plugin.go:201] device plugin handshake failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
Mar 18 10:13:13 kubelet[1234]: W0318 10:13:13 node_status.go:240] Node not ready, setting taint node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule
```

ash: important detail — these nodes are a mix of preemptible and standard VMs. preemptibles are spiking recreations in the pool which makes a global daemonset restart risky.

samir: short-term mitigation idea: temporarily relax the autoscaler's scaleDown/scaleUp filters so it can create fresh nodes in a different pool (non-preemptible) and we move workloads while we fix drivers. that buys time but increases cost.

jess: alternative emergency patch: bump device-plugin daemonset to image with a retry/backoff wrapper that waits for /proc/driver/nvidia up to 2m, plus increase livenessProbe initialDelay. This prevents immediate crash-loop and keeps nodes Ready while driver init completes. low-risk and cheaper than force-scaling to on-demand.

ken: ok action plan:
- step 1 (now): patch device-plugin image -> nv-device-plugin:2026-03-17-hotfix which adds retries and 120s init delay. kubectl apply -n kube-system.
- step 2: increase daemonset rolling update partition to 1 (do one node at a time) and monitor node readiness.
- step 3: for nodes already NotReady, cordon + drain (--ignore-daemonsets) and reboot if device plugin never recovers.
- step 4 (if still failing): instruct autoscaler to prefer non-preemptible pool and scale up a handful of healthy nodes.

maria: patch applied to device-plugin. rollingUpdateStrategy.partition=1. starting with ip-10-0-3-21.

infra-bot: [INFO] Rollout started: ds/nvidia-device-plugin namespace=kube-system by maria at 10:28 UTC

ken: monitor checks: watch kubectl get nodes - we need to see Ready counts climb and taints cleared. also check kubelet journal for modprobe success.

maria: after the patch one of the nodes popped back to Ready after ~90s, device-plugin stayed up. moving to next node. :thumbsup:

ash: good. cost note — if we end up shifting to non-preemptible emergency pool we'll likely double GPU hourly spend for the next 6-12 hours. ops FYI.

samir: follow-up: we should add a preflight on driver images that runs a modprobe test across a sample of kernels/ami variants before fleet rollout. I'll open a quick RFC for an automated smoke test job.

jess: and add a safer rollingStrategy with maxUnavailable=1 and a pre-sleep between pods to avoid N devices going offline in same AZ.

maria: logging this thread and the mitigation steps. will keep this thread updated as we finish the pool. thanks everyone. :coffee:
